findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice when sharding is combined with query splitting
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target before sharding (line 52), exactly as before. However, splitQueriesByStreamShard() still delegates execution of each shard group to `runSplitQuery()` (imported from './querySplitting', used at line 163), and that function has been changed in this PR to also call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on its targets (querySplitting.ts, line 299) before doing its own time-based splitting. Because the sub-request passed into the nested `runSplitQuery()` call still carries the same `request.scopedVars`/`request.filters` and an already-interpolated, shard-labeled `expr`, template-variable interpolation (including ad-hoc filter injection via `request.filters`) now runs a second time on an expression that has already been fully interpolated and had the `__stream_shard__` selector injected. If `applyTemplateVariables` unconditionally appends ad-hoc filters to the expression (a common implementation pattern), this will duplicate label matchers in the final query sent to the backend whenever ad-hoc filters are configured on the dashboard, silently breaking filtering for sharded+split Loki queries. Even if duplication is harmless in the specific implementation, the double interpolation is wasted work and a correctness risk that should be either avoided (skip re-interpolation for already-interpolated sub-requests) or explicitly verified not to double-apply filters/macros.

findings.title: New tests don't verify that filters/macros are not double-applied when sharding delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test (and the updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test, which now simply asserts `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times) mock `datasource.applyTemplateVariables`/`replace` with simple, idempotent string substitutions and never exercise `request.filters` (ad-hoc filters). Because the production code now calls `applyTemplateVariables` twice for every shard group (once in `runShardSplitQuery`, once inside the nested `runSplitQuery` call), a scenario where ad-hoc filters are present is never tested, so a regression that duplicates ad-hoc filter label matchers in the final sharded query would not be caught by this test suite.
